package borg.trikeshed.reactor.http

import borg.trikeshed.reactor.AsyncReaction
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.SelectionKey
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.UnaryAsyncReaction

class HttpServer(private val port: Int) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    private val serverChannel = ServerChannel()

    init {
        serverChannel.bind(port)
    }

    override fun onAccept(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val clientChannel = key.channel.accept()
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) {
            val request = parseRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            val response = handleRequest(request, key)
            OP_READ()
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun parseRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
        val requestLine = bytes.toSeries().asString()
        return HttpRequest(
            method = HttpMethod.GET,
            path = HttpRequestPath("/"),
            headers = emptyMap(),
            body = bytes.toSeries()
        )
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: HttpRequest, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\n\r\nHello World!"
        key.channel.write(response.toByteArray())
        return null
    }
}
```

```
package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>

data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: HttpRequestPath,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val requestLine = "$method $path HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$requestLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}

data class HttpResponse(
    val statusCode: Int,
    val reasonPhrase: String,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val statusLine = "HTTP/1.1 $statusCode $reasonPhrase\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$statusLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}
```

package borg.trikeshed.reactor

import borg.trikeshed.platform.AppDispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import borg.trikeshed.platform.SelectorInterface

class Reactor(
    private val selector: SelectorInterface,
    private val reactions: MutableMap<SelectableChannel, AsyncReaction> = mutableMapOf(),
    private val job: Job = Job(),
    private val scope: CoroutineScope = CoroutineScope(job + AppDispatchers.IO),
    private val bufferPool: BufferPool = BufferPoolImpl()
) {
    private val commandChannel = Channel<Command>(Channel.UNLIMITED)

    init {
        start()
    }

    private fun start() {
        scope.launch {
            while (job.isActive) {
                selector.select()
                val selectedKeys = selector.selectedKeys()
                for (key in selectedKeys) {
                    val reaction = reactions[key.channel]
                    if (reaction != null) {
                        val newReaction = when {
                            key.isReadable() -> reaction.onRead(key)
                            key.isWritable() -> reaction.onWrite(key)
                            key.isConnectable() -> reaction.onConnect(key)
                            key.isAcceptable() -> reaction.onAccept(key)
                            else -> null
                        }
                        if (newReaction != null) {
                            reactions[key.channel] = newReaction
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    internal class BufferPoolImpl : BufferPool {
        override fun acquire(size: Int): Series<Byte> = TODO("Not yet implemented")
        override fun release(buffer: Series<Byte>) = TODO("Not yet implemented")
    }
}
```

package borg.trikeshed.reactor.http

import borg.trikeshed.reactor.AsyncReaction
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.SelectionKey
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.UnaryAsyncReaction

class HttpServer(private val port: Int) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    private val serverChannel = ServerChannel()

    init {
        serverChannel.bind(port)
    }

    override fun onAccept(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val clientChannel = key.channel.accept()
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) {
            val request = parseRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            val response = handleRequest(request, key)
            OP_READ()
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun parseRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
        val requestLine = bytes.toSeries().asString()
        return HttpRequest(
            method = HttpMethod.GET,
            path = HttpRequestPath("/"),
            headers = emptyMap(),
            body = bytes.toSeries()
        )
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: HttpRequest, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\n\r\nHello World!"
        key.channel.write(response.toByteArray())
        return null
    }
}
```

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/HttpTypes.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>

data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: HttpRequestPath,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val requestLine = "$method $path HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$requestLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}

data class HttpResponse(
    val statusCode: Int,
    val reasonPhrase: String,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val statusLine = "HTTP/1.1 $statusCode $reasonPhrase\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$statusLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}
```

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/Reactor.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.reactor

import borg.trikeshed.platform.AppDispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import borg.trikeshed.platform.SelectorInterface

class Reactor(
    private val selector: SelectorInterface,
    private val reactions: MutableMap<SelectableChannel, AsyncReaction> = mutableMapOf(),
    private val job: Job = Job(),
    private val scope: CoroutineScope = CoroutineScope(job + AppDispatchers.IO),
    private val bufferPool: BufferPool = BufferPoolImpl()
) {
    private val commandChannel = Channel<Command>(Channel.UNLIMITED)

    init {
        start()
    }

    private fun start() {
        scope.launch {
            while (job.isActive) {
                selector.select()
                val selectedKeys = selector.selectedKeys()
                for (key in selectedKeys) {
                    val reaction = reactions[key.channel]
                    if (reaction != null) {
                        val newReaction = when {
                            key.isReadable() -> reaction.onRead(key)
                            key.isWritable() -> reaction.onWrite(key)
                            key.isConnectable() -> reaction.onConnect(key)
                            key.isAcceptable() -> reaction.onAccept(key)
                            else -> null
                        }
                        if (newReaction != null) {
                            reactions[key.channel] = newReaction
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    internal class BufferPoolImpl : BufferPool {
        override fun acquire(size: Int): Series<Byte> = TODO("Not yet implemented")
        override fun release(buffer: Series<Byte>) = TODO("Not yet implemented")
    }
}
```

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/Reactor.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.reactor

import borg.trikeshed.platform.AppDispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import borg.trikeshed.platform.SelectorInterface

class Reactor(
    private val selector: SelectorInterface,
    private val reactions: MutableMap<SelectableChannel, AsyncReaction> = mutableMapOf(),
    private val job: Job = Job(),
    private val scope: CoroutineScope = CoroutineScope(job + AppDispatchers.IO),
    private val bufferPool: BufferPool = BufferPoolImpl()
) {
    private val commandChannel = Channel<Command>(Channel.UNLIMITED)

    init {
        start()
    }

    private fun start() {
        scope.launch {
            while (job.isActive) {
                selector.select()
                val selectedKeys = selector.selectedKeys()
                for (key in selectedKeys) {
                    val reaction = reactions[key.channel]
                    if (reaction != null) {
                        val newReaction = when {
                            key.isReadable() -> reaction.onRead(key)
                            key.isWritable() -> reaction.onWrite(key)
                            key.isConnectable() -> reaction.onConnect(key)
                            key.isAcceptable() -> reaction.onAccept(key)
                            else -> null
                        }
                        if (newReaction != null) {
                            reactions[key.channel] = newReaction
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    internal class BufferPoolImpl : BufferPool {
        override fun acquire(size: Int): Series<Byte> = TODO("Not yet implemented")
        override fun release(buffer: Series<Byte>) = TODO("Not yet implemented")
    }
}
```

package borg.trikeshed.reactor.http

import borg.trikeshed.reactor.AsyncReaction
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.SelectionKey
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.UnaryAsyncReaction

class HttpServer(private val port: Int) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    private val serverChannel = ServerChannel()

    init {
        serverChannel.bind(port)
    }

    override fun onAccept(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val clientChannel = key.channel.accept()
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) {
            val request = parseRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            val response = handleRequest(request, key)
            OP_READ()
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun parseRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
        val requestLine = bytes.toSeries().asString()
        return HttpRequest(
            method = HttpMethod.GET,
            path = HttpRequestPath("/"),
            headers = emptyMap(),
            body = bytes.toSeries()
        )
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: HttpRequest, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\n\r\nHello World!"
        key.channel.write(response.toByteArray())
        return null
    }
}
```

package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>

data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: HttpRequestPath,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val requestLine = "$method $path HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$requestLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}

data class HttpResponse(
    val statusCode: Int,
    val reasonPhrase: String,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val statusLine = "HTTP/1.1 $statusCode $reasonPhrase\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$statusLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/Reactor.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.reactor

import borg.trikeshed.platform.AppDispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import borg.trikeshed.platform.SelectorInterface

class Reactor(
    private val selector: SelectorInterface,
    private val reactions: MutableMap<SelectableChannel, AsyncReaction> = mutableMapOf(),
    private val job: Job = Job(),
    private val scope: CoroutineScope = CoroutineScope(job + AppDispatchers.IO),
    private val bufferPool: BufferPool = BufferPoolImpl()
) {
    private val commandChannel = Channel<Command>(Channel.UNLIMITED)

    init {
        start()
    }

    private fun start() {
        scope.launch {
            while (job.isActive) {
                selector.select()
                val selectedKeys = selector.selectedKeys()
                for (key in selectedKeys) {
                    val reaction = reactions[key.channel]
                    if (reaction != null) {
                        val newReaction = when {
                            key.isReadable() -> reaction.onRead(key)
                            key.isWritable() -> reaction.onWrite(key)
                            key.isConnectable() -> reaction.onConnect(key)
                            key.isAcceptable() -> reaction.onAccept(key)
                            else -> null
                        }
                        if (newReaction != null) {
                            reactions[key.channel] = newReaction
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    internal class BufferPoolImpl : BufferPool {
        override fun acquire(size: Int): Series<Byte> = TODO("Not yet implemented")
        override fun release(buffer: Series<Byte>) = TODO("Not yet implemented")
    }
}
```

package borg.trikeshed.reactor.http

import borg.trikeshed.reactor.AsyncReaction
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.SelectionKey
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.UnaryAsyncReaction

class HttpServer(private val port: Int) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    private val serverChannel = ServerChannel()

    init {
        serverChannel.bind(port)
    }

    override fun onAccept(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val clientChannel = key.channel.accept()
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) {
            val request = parseRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            val response = handleRequest(request, key)
            OP_READ()
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun parseRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
        val requestLine = bytes.toSeries().asString()
        return HttpRequest(
            method = HttpMethod.GET,
            path = HttpRequestPath("/"),
            headers = emptyMap(),
            body = bytes.toSeries()
        )
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: HttpRequest, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\n\r\nHello World!"
        key.channel.write(response.toByteArray())
        return null
    }
}
```

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/HttpTypes.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>

data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: HttpRequestPath,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val requestLine = "$method $path HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$requestLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}

data class HttpResponse(
    val statusCode: Int,
    val reasonPhrase: String,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val statusLine = "HTTP/1.1 $statusCode $reasonPhrase\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$statusLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}
```

import borg.trikeshed.reactor.SelectionKey

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/Reactor.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.reactor

import borg.trikeshed.platform.AppDispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import borg.trikeshed.platform.SelectorInterface

class Reactor(
    private val selector: SelectorInterface,
    private val reactions: MutableMap<SelectableChannel, AsyncReaction> = mutableMapOf(),
    private val job: Job = Job(),
    private val scope: CoroutineScope = CoroutineScope(job + AppDispatchers.IO),
    private val bufferPool: BufferPool = BufferPoolImpl()
) {
    private val commandChannel = Channel<Command>(Channel.UNLIMITED)

    init {
        start()
    }

    private fun start() {
        scope.launch {
            while (job.isActive) {
                selector.select()
                val selectedKeys = selector.selectedKeys()
                for (key in selectedKeys) {
                    val reaction = reactions[key.channel]
                    if (reaction != null) {
                        val newReaction = when {
                            key.isReadable() -> reaction.onRead(key)
                            key.isWritable() -> reaction.onWrite(key)
                            key.isConnectable() -> reaction.onConnect(key)
                            key.isAcceptable() -> reaction.onAccept(key)
                            else -> null
                        }
                        if (newReaction != null) {
                            reactions[key.channel] = newReaction
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    internal class BufferPoolImpl : BufferPool {
        override fun acquire(size: Int): Series<Byte> = TODO("Not yet implemented")
        override fun release(buffer: Series<Byte>) = TODO("Not yet implemented")
    }
}
```

package borg.trikeshed.reactor.http

import borg.trikeshed.reactor.AsyncReaction
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.SelectionKey
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.UnaryAsyncReaction

class HttpServer(private val port: Int) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    private val serverChannel = ServerChannel()

    init {
        serverChannel.bind(port)
    }

    override fun onAccept(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val clientChannel = key.channel.accept()
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key:SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) {
            val request = parseRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            val response = handleRequest(request, key)
            OP_READ()
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun parseRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
        val requestLine = bytes.toSeries().asString()
        return HttpRequest(
            method = HttpMethod.GET,
            path = HttpRequestPath("/"),
            headers = emptyMap(),
            body = bytes.toSeries()
        )
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: HttpRequest, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\n\r\nHello World!"
        key.channel.write(response.toByteArray())
        return null
    }
}
```

**Trikeshed/src/commonMain/kotlin/borg/trikeshed/reactor/HttpTypes.kt**
```
package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>

data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: HttpRequestPath,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val requestLine = "$method $path HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$requestLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}

data class HttpResponse(
    val statusCode: Int,
    val reasonPhrase: String,
    val headers: HttpHeaders,
    val body: Series<Byte>
) {
    fun toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
        val statusLine = "HTTP/1.1 $statusCode $reasonPhrase\r\n"
        val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
        val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()
        val head = "$statusLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
        return head + bodyBytes
    }
}
```

#### This is a very large number of compilation errors, indicating several systemic issues in the codebase, primarily related to a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) migration or a large-scale refactoring. The errors fall into a few main categories:  
####   
#### 1.  **Platform-Specific Code in `commonMain`**: A significant number of errors are due to using JVM-specific APIs (like `java.net.*`, `java.nio.*`, `runBlocking`) in the common source set, which is not allowed in KMP.  
#### 2.  **Redeclared Types**: Many classes and type aliases (`QuicConfig`, `JsonParser`, etc.) are declared in multiple files, causing conflicts. This often happens when merging modules or files.  
#### 3.  **Missing or Incorrect Dependencies**: The build is missing key libraries (like `kotlinx-serialization`) or references to internal project modules (`couch` library, `JsonImpl`).  
#### 4.  **Type System Mismatches**: There are frequent mismatches between custom types (like `Join<Int, Function1<Int, Byte>>`) and standard types (`ByteArray`), indicating missing conversion utilities.  
#### 5.  **Syntax and Type Inference Errors**: Simple syntax mistakes (`JvmInline` vs `@JvmInline`) and complex lambda expressions where the compiler needs help with type inference.  
####   
#### I will provide a set of fixes to address these foundational issues. The goal is to resolve the architectural problems to allow the project to compile.  
####   
#### ### Fixes and Evolution

#### +actual typealias SocketException = JvmSocketException

#### +    actual fun getLong(): Long = jvmBuffer.long

####   
#### ### Summary of Changes  
####   
#### 1.  **`build.gradle.kts`**:  
####     *   Added the `kotlinx-serialization-json` dependency for `commonMain` and `jvmMain` to resolve serialization-related errors.  
####   
#### 2.  **File Deletions and Merging**:  
####     *   I've provided a diff that effectively merges logic by deleting `Json.kt` and moving its core concepts into `JsonParser.kt`. A similar strategy should be applied to other redeclared files (`QuicConfig`, `PlatformIO`, etc.), but this diff focuses on the most critical changes to get the build passing.  
####   
#### 3.  **Platform Abstraction (`expect`/`actual`)**:  
####     *   Created a new file `platform/Platform.kt` in `commonMain` to hold `expect` declarations for platform-specific APIs like `DatagramSocket`, `ByteBuffer`, `runBlocking`, etc.  
####     *   Created a corresponding `platform/Platform.jvm.kt` in a new `jvmMain` source set to provide the `actual` JVM implementations for these declarations. This is the core fix for the KMP architecture violations.  
####     *   Code in `commonMain` (like `EnhancedQuicConnection.kt`) has been updated to use these new platform-agnostic `expect` types instead of JVM-specific ones.  
####   
#### 4.  **Core Type System (`lib/Series.kt`)**:  
####     *   Created a new utility file to define a `toByteArray()` extension function for your `Series<Byte>` type. This resolves the widespread type mismatch errors where a `ByteArray` was expected.  
####     *   Added a `ByteArray.toSeries()` for convenience.  
####   
#### 5.  **Code-Level Fixes**:  
####     *   **`HttpServer.kt`**: Corrected function calls (e.g., `OP_ACCEPT()`) and used the new `toByteArray()` extension.  
####     *   **`HttpTypes.kt`**: Fixed string conversion to use `play.joinToString("")` which is a safe way to materialize a `Series<Char>`.  
####     *   **`EnhancedQuicConnection.kt`**: Replaced all `java.*` and `Dispatchers.IO` references with the new `expect` declarations from the `platform` package. Stubbed out or simplified some logic that was difficult to make platform-agnostic without a full rewrite (e.g., `createAckFrame`).  
####     *   **`JsonParser.kt`**: Merged concepts from `Json.kt`, fixed incorrect `when` statement logic, and stubbed out some complex parsing functions (`TODO()`) to allow the file to compile. The parsing logic in this file was deeply flawed and needs a proper rewrite, but these changes will fix the immediate compilation errors.  
####     *   **`RequestFactoryServiceImpl.kt`**: Refactored to provide a concrete implementation and stubbed out the missing `CouchClient` dependency to allow compilation.  
####     *   **`TaxonomicStorage.kt`**: Replaced `Gson` calls with `kotlinx.serialization.json` and stubbed out other missing dependencies (`StratifiedJsonStorage`).  
####     *   **`DealService.kt` / `RequestFactoryBroker.kt`**: Corrected `JvmInline` to `@kotlin.jvm.JvmInline`.  
####   
#### ### Next Steps  
####   
#### This set of changes addresses the most critical architectural and syntactical errors. The project should now be in a much better state to compile, especially the `commonMain` module.  
####   
#### 1.  **Complete the `TODO()` stubs**: Many complex or platform-specific functions have been stubbed out. These will need to be implemented correctly.  
#### 2.  **Implement Native `actual`s**: The `macosArm64Main` (and other native targets) will need `actual` implementations for the `expect` declarations in `platform/Platform.kt`. This is a significant task requiring knowledge of native networking APIs.  
#### 3.  **Resolve Missing Dependencies**: The `CouchClient` and other storage-related classes are still missing. You will need to either add the correct internal module dependency or find a suitable third-party library.  
#### 4.  **Review and Refactor Logic**: The JSON parsing logic, in particular, was heavily patched to compile. It needs a thorough review and likely a complete rewrite to be robust. -------------------------   inductively read these and patch them

#### This is a very large number of compilation errors, indicating several systemic issues in the codebase, primarily related to a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) migration or a large-scale refactoring. The errors fall into a few main categories:  
####   
#### 1.  **Platform-Specific Code in `commonMain`**: A significant number of errors are due to using JVM-specific APIs (like `java.net.*`, `java.nio.*`, `runBlocking`) in the common source set, which is not allowed in KMP.  
#### 2.  **Redeclared Types**: Many classes and type aliases (`QuicConfig`, `JsonParser`, etc.) are declared in multiple files, causing conflicts. This often happens when merging modules or files.  
#### 3.  **Missing or Incorrect Dependencies**: The build is missing key libraries (like `kotlinx-serialization`) or references to internal project modules (`couch` library, `JsonImpl`).  
#### 4.  **Type System Mismatches**: There are frequent mismatches between custom types (like `Join<Int, Function1<Int, Byte>>`) and standard types (`ByteArray`), indicating missing conversion utilities.  
#### 5.  **Syntax and Type Inference Errors**: Simple syntax mistakes (`JvmInline` vs `@JvmInline`) and complex lambda expressions where the compiler needs help with type inference.  
####   
#### I will provide a set of fixes to address these foundational issues. The goal is to resolve the architectural problems to allow the project to compile.  
####   
#### ### Fixes and Evolution

####   
#### ### Summary of Changes  
####   
#### 1.  **`build.gradle.kts`**:  
####     *   Added the `kotlinx-serialization-json` dependency for `commonMain` and `jvmMain` to resolve serialization-related errors.  
####   
#### 2.  **File Deletions and Merging**:  
####     *   I've provided a diff that effectively merges logic by deleting `Json.kt` and moving its core concepts into `JsonParser.kt`. A similar strategy should be applied to other redeclared files (`QuicConfig`, `PlatformIO`, etc.), but this diff focuses on the most critical changes to get the build passing.  
####   
#### 3.  **Platform Abstraction (`expect`/`actual`)**:  
####     *   Created a new file `platform/Platform.kt` in `commonMain` to hold `expect` declarations for platform-specific APIs like `DatagramSocket`, `ByteBuffer`, `runBlocking`, etc.  
####     *   Created a corresponding `platform/Platform.jvm.kt` in a new `jvmMain` source set to provide the `actual` JVM implementations for these declarations. This is the core fix for the KMP architecture violations.  
####     *   Code in `commonMain` (like `EnhancedQuicConnection.kt`) has been updated to use these new platform-agnostic `expect` types instead of JVM-specific ones.  
####   
#### 4.  **Core Type System (`lib/Series.kt`)**:  
####     *   Created a new utility file to define a `toByteArray()` extension function for your `Series<Byte>` type. This resolves the widespread type mismatch errors where a `ByteArray` was expected.  
####     *   Added a `ByteArray.toSeries()` for convenience.  
####   
#### 5.  **Code-Level Fixes**:  
####     *   **`HttpServer.kt`**: Corrected function calls (e.g., `OP_ACCEPT()`) and used the new `toByteArray()` extension.  
####     *   **`HttpTypes.kt`**: Fixed string conversion to use `play.joinToString("")` which is a safe way to materialize a `Series<Char>`.  
####     *   **`EnhancedQuicConnection.kt`**: Replaced all `java.*` and `Dispatchers.IO` references with the new `expect` declarations from the `platform` package. Stubbed out or simplified some logic that was difficult to make platform-agnostic without a full rewrite (e.g., `createAckFrame`).  
####     *   **`JsonParser.kt`**: Merged concepts from `Json.kt`, fixed incorrect `when` statement logic, and stubbed out some complex parsing functions (`TODO()`) to allow the file to compile. The parsing logic in this file was deeply flawed and needs a proper rewrite, but these changes will fix the immediate compilation errors.  
####     *   **`RequestFactoryServiceImpl.kt`**: Refactored to provide a concrete implementation and stubbed out the missing `CouchClient` dependency to allow compilation.  
####     *   **`TaxonomicStorage.kt`**: Replaced `Gson` calls with `kotlinx.serialization.json` and stubbed out other missing dependencies (`StratifiedJsonStorage`).  
####     *   **`DealService.kt` / `RequestFactoryBroker.kt`**: Corrected `JvmInline` to `@kotlin.jvm.JvmInline`.  
####   
#### ### Next Steps  
####   
#### This set of changes addresses the most critical architectural and syntactical errors. The project should now be in a much better state to compile, especially the `commonMain` module.

#### 1.  **Complete the `TODO()` stubs**: Many complex or platform-specific functions have been stubbed out. These will need to be implemented correctly.  
#### 2.  **Implement Native `actual`s**: The `macosArm64Main` (and other native targets) will need `actual` implementations for the `expect` declarations in `platform/Platform.kt`. This is a significant task requiring knowledge of native networking APIs.  
#### 3.  **Resolve Missing Dependencies**: The `CouchClient` and other storage-related classes are still missing. You will need to either add the correct internal module dependency or find a suitable third-party library.

package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.toByteArray
import borg.trikeshed.net.http.HttpServer.ConnectionState.*
import borg.trikeshed.net.http.HttpServer.ConnectionState.Companion.invoke
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.*
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.Interest.Companion.OP_ACCEPT
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.Interest.Companion.OP_READ
import borg.trikeshed.reactor.Interest.Companion.OP_WRITE
import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series
import borg.trikeshed.lib.toSeries

val Series<Char>.toRequest: HttpRequest
    get() = TODO()

class HttpServer(
    private val port: Int,
    private val reaction: UnaryAsyncReaction
) {
    private var serverChannel: ServerChannel? = null
    private var reactor: Reactor? = null

    fun start() {
        serverChannel = ServerChannel()
        serverChannel?.bind(port)

        reactor = Reactor(serverChannel!!, reaction)
        reactor?.start()
    }

    fun stop() {
        reactor?.stop()
        serverChannel?.close()
    }

    sealed class ConnectionState {
        abstract fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction?

        companion object {
            operator fun invoke(): ConnectionState = Idle
        }

        object Idle : ConnectionState() {
            override fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction? {
                return ReadRequestLine.next(key, buffer)
            }
        }

        object ReadRequestLine : ConnectionState() {
            override fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction? {
                return ReadHeaders.next(key, buffer)
            }
        }

        object ReadHeaders : ConnectionState() {
            override fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction? {
                return ProcessRequest.next(key, buffer)
            }
        }

        object ProcessRequest : ConnectionState() {
            override fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction? {
                return WriteResponse.next(key, buffer)
            }
        }

        object WriteResponse : ConnectionState() {
            override fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction? {
                return CloseConnection.next(key, buffer)
            }
        }

        object CloseConnection : ConnectionState() {
            override fun next(key: SelectionKey, buffer: Series<Byte>): AsyncReaction? {
                key.channel.close()
                return null
            }
        }
    }
}

class HttpMotdReaction(
    private val motd: String
) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    override fun onAccept(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        // Simplified: just write the MOTD and close.
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: ${motd.length}\r\n\r\n$motd"
        key.channel.write(response.encodeToByteArray().toSeries())
        return OP_READ()
    }
}

class HttpStateMachine : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    override fun onAccept(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) OP_READ() {
            val request = parseRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            handleRequest(request, key)
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: String, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 12\r\n\r\nHello World!"
        key.channel.write(response.toByteArray())
        // After writing, we might want to close or wait for more requests.
        return OP_WRITE() { null }
    }

    private fun parseRequest(bytes: ByteArray): String {
        return bytes.decodeToString()
    }
}

class HttpRouter(
    private val routes: Map<String, (HttpRequest) -> HttpResponse>
) : UnaryAsyncReaction {
    override fun onAccept(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        return OP_ACCEPT()
    }

    override fun onRead(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val buffer = ByteArray(1024)
        val read = key.channel.read(buffer.toSeries())
        return if (read > 0) OP_READ() {
            val request = parseHttpRequest(buffer.sliceArray(0 until read))
            handleRequest(request, key)
        } else {
            null
        }
    }

    private fun handleRequest(request: HttpRequest, key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val handler = routes[request.path] ?: return sendNotFound(key)
        val response = handler(request)
        key.channel.write(response.toHttpMessage().toByteArray())
        return OP_WRITE() { null }
    }

    private fun sendNotFound(key: SelectionKey): AsyncReaction? {
        val response = HttpResponse(
            version = "HTTP/1.1",
            statusCode = 404,
            reasonPhrase = "Not Found"
        )
        key.channel.write(response.toHttpMessage().toByteArray())
        return OP_WRITE() { null }
    }

    private fun parseHttpRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
        return HttpRequest.parse(bytes)
    }
}

fun main() {
    val motd = "Hello, World!"
    val reaction = HttpMotdReaction(motd)
    val server = HttpServer(8080, reaction)
    server.start()
}

package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series
import borg.trikeshed.lib.toSeries

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>

// HTTP Method enumeration
enum class HttpMethod {
    GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, COPY, TRACE, CONNECT
}

// HTTP Request data class (RFC 7230 compliant)
data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: String,
    val headers: Map<String, Series<Char>>,
    val body: Series<Byte>? = null,
    val version: String = "HTTP/1.1"
)

// HTTP Response data class (RFC 7230 compliant)
data class HttpResponse(
    val version: String = "HTTP/1.1",
    val statusCode: Int,
    val reasonPhrase: String,
    val headers: Map<String, Series<Char>> = emptyMap(),
    val body: Series<Byte>? = null
)

fun HttpResponse.toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
    val statusLine = "$version $statusCode $reasonPhrase\r\n"
    val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
    val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()

    val head = "$statusLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
    return head + bodyBytes
}

fun parseHttpRequest(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
    val lines = bytes.decodeToString().split("\r\n")
    val (method, path, version) = lines[0].split(" ", limit = 3)

    val headers = mutableMapOf<String, Series<Char>>()
    lines.drop(1).takeWhile { it.isNotEmpty() }.forEach { line ->
        val (key, value) = line.split(":", limit = 2)
        headers[key.trim()] = value.trim().toSeries() as Series<Char>
    }

    // Body parsing is complex and depends on headers (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding)
    return HttpRequest(
        method = HttpMethod.valueOf(method),
        path = path,
        headers = headers,
        version = version
    )
}

fun HttpRequest.toHttpMessage(): Series<Byte> {
    val requestLine = "$method $path $version\r\n"
    val headersStr = headers.map { (k, v) -> "$k: ${v.play.joinToString("")}" }.joinToString("\r\n")
    val bodyBytes = body ?: ByteArray(0).toSeries()

    val head = "$requestLine$headersStr\r\n\r\n".toSeries().map { it.code.toByte() }.toSeries()
    return head + bodyBytes
}

package borg.trikeshed.net.quic

import borg.trikeshed.platform.AppDispatchers
import borg.trikeshed.platform.ByteBuffer
import borg.trikeshed.platform.ConcurrentHashMap
import borg.trikeshed.platform.DatagramPacket
import borg.trikeshed.platform.DatagramSocket
import borg.trikeshed.platform.InetSocketAddress
import borg.trikeshed.platform.SocketException
import borg.trikeshed.platform.Volatile
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.receiveAsFlow

open class QuicConnection(
    private val remoteAddress: InetSocketAddress,
    private val config: QuicConfig,
    private val sessionCache: QuicSessionCache = InMemoryQuicSessionCache()
) {
    private var socket: DatagramSocket? = null
    private val streams = ConcurrentHashMap<Long, QuicStream>()
    private val internalReceiveChannel = Channel<ByteArray>(Channel.BUFFERED)
    private val job = kotlinx.coroutines.SupervisorJob()
    private val scope = kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope(AppDispatchers.IO + job)

    val isConnected: Boolean
        get() = socket?.isConnected == true

    @Volatile
    var isClosed: Boolean = false
        private set

    init {
        // Simplified logging
        println("Creating new QUIC connection to ${remoteAddress} with config: ${config}")
    }

    fun connect() {
        if (isConnected) return
        socket = DatagramSocket()
        socket?.connect(remoteAddress)
        startReceiverJob()
        startHeartbeatJob()
    }

    fun send(streamId: Long, data: ByteArray) {
        val stream = streams.computeIfAbsent(streamId) {
            QuicStream(streamId, this, config.initialStreamFlowControlWindow)
        }
        scope.launch(AppDispatchers.IO) {
            stream.send(data)
        }
    }

    fun receive(): Flow<ByteArray> {
        return internalReceiveChannel.receiveAsFlow()
    }

    private fun startHeartbeatJob() {
        scope.launch(AppDispatchers.IO) {
            while (isActive) {
                delay(config.idleTimeout.toLong() / 2)
                sendPing()
            }
        }
    }

    fun close() {
        socket?.close()
        job.cancel()
    }

    private fun startReceiverJob() {
        if (socket == null || isClosed) return
        scope.launch(AppDispatchers.IO) {
            val buffer = ByteArray(config.maxPacketSize)
            val packet = DatagramPacket(buffer, buffer.size)
            while (isActive) {
                try {
                    socket?.receive(packet)
                    processReceivedPacket(packet.data)
                } catch (e: SocketException) {
                    if (!isClosed) {
                        println("Socket error: ${e.message}")
                    }
                    break
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private fun sendPacket(data: ByteArray) {
        scope.launch(AppDispatchers.IO) {
            val packet = DatagramPacket(data, data.size, remoteAddress)
            socket?.send(packet)
        }
    }

    private fun processReceivedPacket(packet: ByteArray) {
        val buffer = ByteBuffer.wrap(packet)
        val streamId = buffer.getLong() // Assuming ByteBuffer has getLong
        val stream = streams[streamId]
        if (stream != null) {
            val data = ByteArray(buffer.remaining())
            buffer.get(data)
            stream.receive(data)
        }
    }

    private fun sendPing() {
        scope.launch(AppDispatchers.IO) {
            val pingFrame = createPingFrame()
            val packet = DatagramPacket(pingFrame, pingFrame.size, remoteAddress)
            socket?.send(packet)
        }
    }
}

private fun createPingFrame(): ByteArray = byteArrayOf(0x01)

package borg.trikeshed.net.quic

import borg.trikeshed.platform.ConcurrentHashMap
import borg.trikeshed.platform.System

class InMemoryQuicSessionCache : QuicSessionCache {
    private val cache = ConcurrentHashMap<String, QuicSessionData>()

    override fun get(key: String): QuicSessionData? {
        val data = cache[key]
        if (data != null && System.currentTimeMillis() > data.expirationTime) {
            cache.remove(key)
            return null // Correct
        }
        return data
    }

    override fun put(key: String, data: QuicSessionData) {
        cache[key] = data
    }
}

#### This is a very large number of compilation errors, indicating several systemic issues in the codebase, primarily related to a Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) migration or a large-scale refactoring. The errors fall into a few main categories:  
####   
#### 1.  **Platform-Specific Code in `commonMain`**: A significant number of errors are due to using JVM-specific APIs (like `java.net.*`, `java.nio.*`, `runBlocking`) in the common source set, which is not allowed in KMP.  
#### 2.  **Redeclared Types**: Many classes and type aliases (`QuicConfig`, `JsonParser`, etc.) are declared in multiple files, causing conflicts. This often happens when merging modules or files.  
#### 3.  **Missing or Incorrect Dependencies**: The build is missing key libraries (like `kotlinx-serialization`) or references to internal project modules (`couch` library, `JsonImpl`).  
#### 4.  **Type System Mismatches**: There are frequent mismatches between custom types (like `Join<Int, Function1<Int, Byte>>`) and standard types (`ByteArray`), indicating missing conversion utilities.  
#### 5.  **Syntax and Type Inference Errors**: Simple syntax mistakes (`JvmInline` vs `@JvmInline`) and complex lambda expressions where the compiler needs help with type inference.  
####

#### 1.  **Platform-Specific Code in `commonMain`**: A significant number of errors are due to using JVM-specific APIs (like `java.net.*`, `java.nio.*`, `runBlocking`) in the common source set, which is not allowed in KMP.  
#### 2.  **Redeclared Types**: Many classes and type aliases (`QuicConfig`, `JsonParser`, etc.) are declared in multiple files, causing conflicts. This often happens when merging modules or files.  
#### 3.  **Missing or Incorrect Dependencies**: The build is missing key libraries (like `kotlinx-serialization`) or references to internal project modules (`couch` library, `JsonImpl`).  
#### 4.  **Type System Mismatches**: There are frequent mismatches between custom types (like `Join<Int, Function1<Int, Byte>>`) and standard types (`ByteArray`), indicating missing conversion utilities.  
#### 5.  **Syntax and Type Inference Errors**: Simple syntax mistakes (`JvmInline` vs `@JvmInline`) and complex lambda expressions where the compiler needs help with type inference.

#### +package borg.trikeshed.platform  
#### +  
#### +import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineDispatcher  
#### +import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers  
#### +import java.net.DatagramPacket as JvmDatagramPacket  
#### +import java.net.DatagramSocket as JvmDatagramSocket  
#### +import java.net.InetSocketAddress as JvmInetSocketAddress  
#### +import java.net.SocketException as JvmSocketException  
#### +import java.nio.ByteBuffer as JvmByteBuffer  
#### +import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap as JvmConcurrentHashMap  
#### +  
#### +actual typealias DatagramSocket = JvmDatagramSocket  
#### +actual typealias DatagramPacket = JvmDatagramPacket  
#### +actual typealias InetSocketAddress = JvmInetSocketAddress  
#### +actual typealias SocketException = JvmSocketException  
#### +  
#### +actual typealias Volatile = kotlin.jvm.Volatile  
#### +actual typealias ConcurrentHashMap<K, V> = JvmConcurrentHashMap<K, V>  
#### +  
#### +actual object AppDispatchers {  
#### +    actual val IO: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.IO  
#### +}  
#### +  
#### +actual fun <T> runBlocking(block: suspend kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope.() -> T): T = kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO, block)  
#### +  
#### +actual class ByteBuffer(private val jvmBuffer: JvmByteBuffer) {  
#### +    actual fun remaining(): Int = jvmBuffer.remaining()  
#### +    actual fun getLong(): Long = jvmBuffer.long  
#### +    actual fun get(dst: ByteArray) = jvmBuffer.get(dst)  
#### +  
#### +    actual companion object {  
#### +        actual fun wrap(array: ByteArray): ByteBuffer = ByteBuffer(JvmByteBuffer.wrap(array))  
#### +    }  
#### +}

####   
#### ### Summary of Changes  
####   
#### 1.  **`build.gradle.kts`**:  
####     *   Added the `kotlinx-serialization-json` dependency for `commonMain` and `jvmMain` to resolve serialization-related errors.  
####   
#### 2.  **File Deletions and Merging**:  
####     *   I've provided a diff that effectively merges logic by deleting `Json.kt` and moving its core concepts into `JsonParser.kt`. A similar strategy should be applied to other redeclared files (`QuicConfig`, `PlatformIO`, etc.), but this diff focuses on the most critical changes to get the build passing.  
####   
#### 3.  **Platform Abstraction (`expect`/`actual`)**:  
####     *   Created a new file `platform/Platform.kt` in `commonMain` to hold `expect` declarations for platform-specific APIs like `DatagramSocket`, `ByteBuffer`, `runBlocking`, etc.  
####     *   Created a corresponding `platform/Platform.jvm.kt` in a new `jvmMain` source set to provide the `actual` JVM implementations for these declarations. This is the core fix for the KMP architecture violations.  
####     *   Code in `commonMain` (like `EnhancedQuicConnection.kt`) has been updated to use these new platform-agnostic `expect` types instead of JVM-specific ones.  
####   
#### 4.  **Core Type System (`lib/Series.kt`)**:  
####     *   Created a new utility file to define a `toByteArray()` extension function for your `Series<Byte>` type. This resolves the widespread type mismatch errors where a `ByteArray` was expected.  
####     *   Added a `ByteArray.toSeries()` for convenience.  
####   
#### 5.  **Code-Level Fixes**:  
####     *   **`HttpServer.kt`**: Corrected function calls (e.g., `OP_ACCEPT()`) and used the new `toByteArray()` extension.  
####     *   **`HttpTypes.kt`**: Fixed string conversion to use `play.joinToString("")` which is a safe way to materialize a `Series<Char>`.

package borg.trikeshed.net.http

import borg.trikeshed.lib.Series
import borg.trikeshed.lib.toSeries

typealias HttpHeaders = Map<String, Series<Char>>
typealias HttpMessageBody = Series<Byte>

// Ontological HTTP Type Aliases
@JvmInline value class HttpHeaderName(val value: String)
@JvmInline value class HttpHeaderValue(val value: String)
@JvmInline value class HttpRequestPath(val value: String)
@JvmInline value class HttpStatusCode(val value: Int)
@JvmInline value class HttpReasonPhrase(val value: String)
@JvmInline value class HttpVersion(val value: String)

// HTTP Method enumeration
enum class HttpMethod {
    GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, COPY, TRACE, CONNECT
}

// HTTP Request data class (RFC 7230 compliant)
data class HttpRequest(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val path: HttpRequestPath,
    val headers: Series<Join<HttpHeaderName, HttpHeaderValue>>,
    val body: ByteArray = byteArrayOf(),
    val version: HttpVersion = HttpVersion("HTTP/1.1")
) {
    fun toByteArray(): ByteArray {
        val startLine = "${method.name} ${path.value} ${version.value}\r\n"
        val headersStr = StringBuilder()
        (0 until headers.a).forEach { i ->
            val header = headers.b(i)
            headersStr.append("${header.a.value}: ${header.b.value}\r\n")
        }
        val finalHeaders = headersStr.toString()
        val head = (startLine + finalHeaders + "\r\n").encodeToByteArray()
        return head + body
    }

    companion object {
        fun parse(bytes: ByteArray): HttpRequest {
            val eoh = findEndOfHeaders(bytes)
            val headerBytes = bytes.sliceArray(0 until eoh)
            val bodyBytes = bytes.sliceArray(eoh + 4 until bytes.size)

            val headerLines = headerBytes.decodeToString().split("\r\n")
            val startLineParts = headerLines[0].split(" ", limit = 3)

            val method = HttpMethod.valueOf(startLineParts[0])
            val path = HttpRequestPath(startLineParts[1])
            val version = HttpVersion(startLineParts[2])

            val headersList = mutableListOf<Join<HttpHeaderName, HttpHeaderValue>>()
            for (i in 1 until headerLines.size) {
                if (headerLines[i].isBlank()) continue
                val headerParts = headerLines[i].split(":", limit = 2)
                headersList.add(Join(HttpHeaderName(headerParts[0].trim()), HttpHeaderValue(headerParts[1].trim())))
            }
            val headers = Series.of(headersList.size) { headersList[it] }

            return HttpRequest(method, path, headers, bodyBytes, version)
        }

        private fun findEndOfHeaders(bytes: ByteArray): Int {
            for (i in 0 until bytes.size - 3) {
                if (bytes[i] == '\r'.code.toByte() && bytes[i + 1] == '\n'.code.toByte() &&
                    bytes[i + 2] == '\r'.code.toByte() && bytes[i + 3] == '\n'.code.toByte()
                ) {
                    return i
                }
            }
            return -1
        }
    }
}

// HTTP Response data class (RFC 7230 compliant)
data class HttpResponse(
    val status: HttpStatusCode,
    val reasonPhrase: HttpReasonPhrase = HttpReasonPhrase("OK"),
    val headers: Series<Join<HttpHeaderName, HttpHeaderValue>>,
    val body: ByteArray = byteArrayOf(),
    val version: HttpVersion = HttpVersion("HTTP/1.1")
) {
    val isSuccess: Boolean get() = status.value in 200..299

    fun toByteArray(): ByteArray {
        val startLine = "${version.value} ${status.value} ${reasonPhrase.value}\r\n"
        val headersStr = StringBuilder()
        (0 until headers.a).forEach { i ->
            val header = headers.b(i)
            headersStr.append("${header.a.value}: ${header.b.value}\r\n")
        }
        val finalHeaders = headersStr.toString()
        val head = (startLine + finalHeaders + "\r\n").encodeToByteArray()
        return head + body
    }

    companion object {
        fun parse(bytes: ByteArray): HttpResponse {
            val eoh = findEndOfHeaders(bytes)
            val headerBytes = bytes.sliceArray(0 until eoh)
            val bodyBytes = bytes.sliceArray(eoh + 4 until bytes.size)

            val headerLines = headerBytes.decodeToString().split("\r\n")
            val startLineParts = headerLines[0].split(" ", limit = 3)

            val version = HttpVersion(startLineParts[0])
            val status = HttpStatusCode(startLineParts[1].toInt())
            val reason = HttpReasonPhrase(startLineParts[2])

            val headersList = mutableListOf<Join<HttpHeaderName, HttpHeaderValue>>()
            for (i in 1 until headerLines.size) {
                if (headerLines[i].isBlank()) continue
                val headerParts = headerLines[i].split(":", limit = 2)
                headersList.add(Join(HttpHeaderName(headerParts[0].trim()), HttpHeaderValue(headerParts[1].trim())))
            }
            val headers = Series.of(headersList.size) { headersList[it] }

            return HttpResponse(status, reason, headers, bodyBytes, version)
        }

        private fun findEndOfHeaders(bytes: ByteArray): Int {
            for (i in 0 until bytes.size - 3) {
                if (bytes[i] == '\r'.code.toByte() && bytes[i + 1] == '\n'.code.toByte() &&
                    bytes[i + 2] == '\r'.code.toByte() && bytes[i + 3] == '\n'.code.toByte()
                ) {
                    return i
                }
            }
            return -1
        }
    }
}

suspend fun HttpRequest.send(): HttpResponse = TODO("HTTP client implementation needed")

// HTTP utilities
object HttpUtils {
    fun parseHeaders(headerString: String): Series<Join<HttpHeaderName, HttpHeaderValue>> {
        val headerLines = headerString.lines().filter { it.contains(":") }
        return Series.of(headerLines.size) { i ->
            val line = headerLines[i]
            val parts = line.split(":", limit = 2)
            Join(HttpHeaderName(parts[0].trim()), HttpHeaderValue(parts[1].trim()))
        }
    }
    
    fun buildHeaderString(headers: Series<Join<HttpHeaderName, HttpHeaderValue>>): String {
        return (0 until headers.a).joinToString("\r\n") { i ->
            val join = headers.b(i)
            "${join.a.value}: ${join.b.value}"
        }
    }
}

// HTTP Message structure for parsing
data class HttpMessage(
    val startLine: HttpStartLine,
    val headerFields: Series<Join<HttpFieldName, HttpFieldValue>>,
    val messageBody: ByteArray
)

sealed interface HttpStartLine
data class HttpRequestLine(
    val method: HttpMethod,
    val requestTarget: HttpRequestTarget,
    val httpVersion: HttpVersion
) : HttpStartLine

data class HttpResponseLine(
    val httpVersion: HttpVersion,
    val statusCode: HttpStatusCode,
    val reasonPhrase: HttpReasonPhrase
) : HttpStartLine

@JvmInline value class HttpRequestTarget(val value: String)
@JvmInline value class HttpFieldName(val value: String)
@JvmInline value class HttpFieldValue(val value: String)

object HttpParser {
    fun parseHttpMessage(message: Series<Char>): HttpMessage? {
        val lines = message.play.joinToString("").split("\r\n")
        if (lines.isEmpty()) return null

        val startLineStr = lines[0]
        val startLine = parseStartLine(startLineStr) ?: return null

        val headerFields = mutableListOf<Join<HttpFieldName, HttpFieldValue>>()
        for (i in 1 until lines.size) {
            val line = lines[i]
            if (line.isBlank()) break // End of headers
            val parts = line.split(":", limit = 2)
            if (parts.size == 2) {
                headerFields.add(HttpFieldName(parts[0].trim()) j HttpFieldValue(parts[1].trim()))
            }
        }

        val bodyStartIndex = lines.indexOfFirst { it.isBlank() } + 1
        val messageBody = if (bodyStartIndex < lines.size) {
            lines.drop(bodyStartIndex).joinToString("\r\n").encodeToByteArray()
        } else {
            byteArrayOf()
        }

        return HttpMessage(startLine, Series.of(headerFields.size) { headerFields[it] }, messageBody)
    }

    private fun parseStartLine(line: String): HttpStartLine? {
        val parts = line.split(" ", limit = 3)
        if (parts.size < 2) return null

        return if (parts[0].startsWith("HTTP/")) { // Response Line
            if (parts.size < 3) return null
            HttpResponseLine(
                HttpVersion(parts[0]),
                HttpStatusCode(parts[1].toIntOrNull() ?: return null),
                HttpReasonPhrase(parts[2])
            )
        } else { // Request Line
            if (parts.size < 3) return null
            HttpRequestLine(
                HttpMethod.valueOf(parts[0]),
                HttpRequestTarget(parts[1]),
                HttpVersion(parts[2])
            )
        }
    }

    // Placeholder for chunked body parsing
    fun parseChunkedBody(input: Series<Char>): ChunkedBody? {
        // This is a complex parsing task, returning a stub for now.
        // A real implementation would parse chunk sizes and data.
        return ChunkedBody(Series.of(0) { Chunk(0, Series.of(0) { 0.toByte() }) })
    }
}

object HttpSerializer {
    fun serializeHttpMessage(message: HttpMessage): Series<Char> {
        val sb = StringBuilder()
        when (message.startLine) {
            is HttpRequestLine -> sb.append("${message.startLine.method.name} ${message.startLine.requestTarget.value} ${message.startLine.httpVersion.value}\r\n")
            is HttpResponseLine -> sb.append("${message.startLine.httpVersion.value} ${message.startLine.statusCode.value} ${message.startLine.reasonPhrase.value}\r\n")
        }

        message.headerFields.play.forEach { header ->
            sb.append("${header.a.value}: ${header.b.value}\r\n")
        }
        sb.append("\r\n") // End of headers

        if (message.messageBody.isNotEmpty()) {
            sb.append(message.messageBody.decodeToString()) // Assuming body is text for simplicity
        }
        return sb.toString().toSeries()
    }
}

data class ChunkedBody(val chunks: Series<Chunk>)
data class Chunk(val size: Int, val data: Series<Byte>)
